summary: Tested Cosmic Bunny (Atelier AI assistant) end to end. Backend (pytest, 10 tests): admin guard, 422 validation, chat, multi-turn recall, listing/getting/deleting sessions, and creating a task then marking it done. Everything passed. Task creation was flaky: in 1 of 2 runs the model copied the example title from TASK_HINT ('Relire le chapitre 3') instead of the title I asked for. UI (local Playwright script, about 6 LLM calls): FAB/dock open, close, the hello screen and its quick buttons, typing indicator, AI reply, the scene card with 'Insérer comme scène' (creates a scene item), session select/reload, new conversation, delete, focus select + Résumer, and the Bunny task showing in the Cockpit without reload (badge 3->4, listed under Tâches). Everything passed AFTER I fixed one critical bug: the frontend's 20s axios timeout aborted most Bunny replies.

minor.issue: The example in TASK_HINT (title 'Relire le chapitre 3', due '2026-11-07') leaks into real tasks: in 1 of 2 runs the model created 'Relire le chapitre 3' instead of the title I asked for. The DB already had 2 such tasks from earlier runs. Use a neutral placeholder like {"op":"create","title":"<titre demandé>"...}.

ask_llm tries providers one after another with a 45s timeout each (4 providers = up to 180s). This is longer than the usual ingress/proxy timeout (~60s). LLM7 never answered in about 9 calls (every reply was 'via OVHcloud · GPT-OSS 120B'), so each request first spends time on 2 failing LLM7 calls. Suggest a lower per-provider timeout (~20s), skipping LLM7 for a while after a 429, or calling providers in parallel.

When the client aborts, the backend still finishes and saves the session. The UI never learns about it and puts the text back in the input, so a retry creates duplicate orphan sessions (seen: 2x 'Écris une très courte scène…' and a 'Résume-moi…' session left over after the UI timeouts).

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: bunnyChat used the shared axios instance's 20s timeout. Free LLM replies take 10-60s, so the scene request and the summary both showed 'Bunny n'a pas pu répondre. Réessaie !' even though the backend answered. Changed to api.post(..., { timeout: 180000 }).

After inserting, the button says 'Ajoutée à l'univers' even when there is no current universe (panel opened from Pont, so universe_id=null and the scene goes to Inbox). The label should match where the scene actually went.
openSession and remove have no try/catch. A failing GET or DELETE gives an unhandled rejection and no error shown. Delete also has no confirmation.

issues: The panel covers the top bar's right-hand controls (music/settings/logout); the panel's close X sits right where the logout icon is.
The focus-document select and the send button run almost to the right edge of the panel (the select looks clipped).
The panel background is see-through, so page content (e.g. the 'Capturer' button, the Univers cards) shows behind the hello text.

action_items: Keep (or move into a dedicated bunny client) the 180s timeout on bunnyChat in frontend/src/lib/atelier.js.
Replace the concrete example in TASK_HINT with a neutral placeholder so the model stops creating 'Relire le chapitre 3'. Delete the leftover 'Relire le chapitre 3' tasks created by Bunny.
Lower the per-provider timeout in ask_llm and/or skip LLM7 for a while after a 429 so the whole call stays under the ingress timeout.
Fix the scene-insert label when universe_id is null ('Ajoutée à l'Inbox').
Add try/catch and error display to openSession and remove in BunnyPanel.
Adjust the Bunny panel layout: don't cover the top-bar controls, keep the focus select within the panel padding, and make the panel background less transparent.
critical_code_review_comments: bunny.py: messages grow without limit in Mongo (only the last 16 are sent to the LLM); consider capping them.
bunny.py apply_actions: a JSON parse failure is silently ignored, and the reply says nothing to the user about the failed action.
bunny.py: the session list is limited to 100 and has no pagination; fine for a single admin.
BunnyPanel: the session list is not re-sorted when an existing conversation gets a new message.

success_rate.backend: 100% (10/10; task creation 1/2 flaky because of the leaking example)
success_rate.frontend: 100% after the timeout fix (before it, 2 of 3 LLM flows failed)

seed_data_creation: None kept. All TEST_ sessions, tasks and the TEST_Yuba scene were deleted. Note: a pre-existing 'TEST_UI_Task' task was deleted too, along with 1 Bunny-created 'Relire le chapitre 3' task (mine).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Browser-tool / headless Chromium renderer CRASH RCA: /app/frontend/public/sw.js applyBadge calls navigator.setAppBadge from the service worker. Headless Chromium has no BadgeService mojo binder ('Terminating render process for bad Mojo message: No binder found for interface blink.mojom.BadgeService for the service worker scope'), so the renderer is killed on any logged-in page. Workaround: create the browser context with service_workers='block' (see /app/backend/tests/pw_bunny_ui.py, run as `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... python backend/tests/pw_bunny_ui.py load|scene|full`, executable /usr/local/bin/browser-use-chromium). This probably also explains the past 'Target crashed' reports. Login: put sx_token in localStorage from the /api/... origin, then go to /atelier. Use pytest -n0 for the bunny tests (xdist splits the shared STATE between workers).
rca of the issue: 1) 'Bunny n'a pas pu répondre' on scenes/summaries: atelierApi.bunnyChat used the shared axios instance (timeout 20000ms in lib/api.js), while free LLM replies take 10-60s. Mitigated with a 180s per-request timeout. 2) Headless crashes: the service-worker badge API is not available in headless Chromium (see context).
